index_record.dataset_generation_caption: The figure illustrates the structure and connectivity of a GraphNode within a modular graph-based system. The global layout is horizontal, centered around a large circular node labeled 'GraphNode' at the top center. This central node contains two smaller square elements: a yellow square on the left and a dark green square on the right. These internal squares are connected by solid vertical lines to labels positioned below the circle: 'source_modules' for the yellow square and 'sink_modules' for the green square, indicating their functional roles within the node. To the left of the GraphNode, two rectangular blocks labeled 'GraphModule' are arranged vertically, each enclosed in a dashed border and filled with light gray. Dashed lines extend from these two GraphModules to the yellow square inside the GraphNode, signifying that they are source modules feeding into this node. On the right side of the GraphNode, a single 'GraphModule' block, also with a dashed border and light gray fill, is connected via a dashed line to the green square, representing a sink module receiving output from the GraphNode. The visual style uses simple geometric shapes—rectangles for modules and a circle for the node—with distinct colors (yellow and green) to differentiate between source and sink components. All connections are represented by dashed lines, suggesting a logical or data flow rather than a physical connection. The figure’s purpose, as stated in the caption, is to demonstrate how a GraphNode functions as a connector within the network, aggregating inputs from source modules and distributing outputs to sink modules. The diagram is clean, minimalistic, and focused on illustrating the directional relationships and modular composition of the system.
